title: Esper framework profile
description: What is specific to a framework, as data: how routes are declared, how middleware chains are built, and what reads the request (D10).

language.description: The language of the code the profile reads.

extends.description: Profiles whose request type, handler adapters, routers, guards and reads also apply: a profile of the same kind when there is one, otherwise of the other kind.

detect.description: How the profile recognises its target: a module that requires a dependency (an application), a module with that path (the framework itself), or a file that imports a package.

request.description: The type of the incoming request, as `<import path>#<Type>`; for TypeScript, a global type is `globalThis#<Type>` and a type of the target is named by its package (`hono#Context` in Hono's own code).

response.description: The type a handler writes its response to, as `<import path>#<Type>`.

context.description: What a handler or a middleware receives first when its code does not state a type: Hono's `hono#Context`.

adapters.description: Conversions and wrappers whose first argument is the handler: `net/http#HandlerFunc`.

types.description: Types of functions that are handlers or middleware (`hono#MiddlewareHandler`): a function typed so receives the `context` first.

aliases.description: Import specifiers a framework maps to a folder of the package that uses it, outside the target's own configuration: `$lib` to `src/lib`, for `$lib` and `$lib/…`.

members.description: The members of types outside the target, which the index cannot read: for each type, the type of each property, so that `({ request }) => …` given a `@sveltejs/kit#RequestEvent` reads a `globalThis#Request`.

returns.description: What functions outside the target return, by symbol: `$app/server#getRequestEvent` returns a `@sveltejs/kit#RequestEvent`.

refusals.description: Calls that answer the request with a refusal (an error, a redirect, a failure), for the guards that are checks.

surface.description: For a framework: what its request surface is. `exported` makes each exported function, and each exported method of an exported type, an entry point when what it reaches reads the request. `handlers` makes each function and method that takes a response writer and the request an entry point, exported or not: the framework's internal handlers. `except` leaves out the files of code that does not serve requests.

except.description: Files whose code is not part of the request surface, as globs from the target's root (`**` any folders, `*` any name): a framework's code that runs in the browser.

guards.description: Middleware and functions that can refuse a request, by the kind of check they make.

mutations.description: What changes request state that later middleware or the handler reads again: chains of fields and calls, as for reads (`set()` on `hono#Context`).

sinks.description: Framework calls that are sinks, by kind, as in a language's library: `<symbol>@<n>` names the argument that is interpreted when it is not the first, `@*` any argument.

types.description: The types a router value has, so that a parameter of one of them receives the router passed to it.

create.description: Functions that return a new router.

default.description: Package functions that register on a router of the package itself, such as `http.HandleFunc` on the default mux.

pattern.description: How a route's path is written: `braces` for `/items/{id}`, `{id:[0-9]+}` and `*`; `servemux` for `GET /items/{id}`, `{path...}` and a trailing `/` for a subtree; `colon` for `/items/:id`, `:id{[0-9]+}`, `:id?` and `*`. `brackets` for a folder of a route tree: `[id]`, `[[optional]]`, `[...rest]`, `[id=matcher]`, and `(group)`, which takes no part in the path.

ordered.description: Middleware applies only to the routes registered after it, and only to those its own path matches (`use('/admin/*', auth)`), as Hono's does; otherwise to every route of the router.

chained.description: Its methods return the router, so that registrations chain: `app.get(…).post(…)`.

registers.description: Routes a package registers on the `default` router when it is imported, even for its side effects alone (`import _ "net/http/pprof"`).

method.description: A method of a router, or a function listed in `default`, by what it does.

does.description: `route` adds a route; `use` adds middleware to the router's chain, after a path when the first argument is one; `with` returns a router with more middleware; `group` passes a router with the same prefix to a callback; `subrouter` passes a router mounted at a prefix to a callback; `mount` attaches a router or a handler at a prefix; `prefix` returns a router whose registrations go to this one under a prefix (Hono's `basePath`).

method.description: For `route`: the HTTP method, `ANY`, or `pattern` when the path carries it (`GET /items`).

args.description: The meaning of each argument, when it is not the default for `does`: `route` takes `[path, handler]`, `subrouter` `[path, callback]`, `group` `[callback]`, `mount` `[path, handler]`, `prefix` `[path]`. `chain` stands for every argument between the ones before it and the last, middleware in front of the handler; `config` for an object whose properties say what `config` maps them to.

config.description: For a `config` argument: the role of each property of the object (`{ method: method, path: path, middleware: chain }`).

through.description: Functions that return the configuration they are given (`@hono/zod-openapi#createRoute`), seen through.

pattern.description: How this method's paths are written, when not as the router's.

read.description: What reads the request: a chain of fields and calls on the request, or on another value that carries it (`Header.Get(name)`, `ctx.Value(name)`), or a function taking it (`chi.URLParam(r, name)`).

chain.description: Fields and calls on the request, in order. `(name)` marks the argument that names what is read; `()` a call whose arguments do not matter; `[name]` a property whose name says what is read, written `.id` or `['id']` (`params[name]`).

request.description: For `call`: the argument that is the request.

name.description: For `call`: the argument that names what is read.

on.description: For `chain`: the type the chain starts from, when it is not the request: `context#Context` for `ctx.Value(key)`.

by.description: For `chain`: the kind of read named by the string its `(name)` argument holds, rather than `read` with that name: `req.valid(name)` reads the body for `json` and a path parameter for `param`.

guard.description: A call that can refuse a request (`basicAuth`), or a check: a function that refuses the request, by one of the profile's `refusals`, when a value read from it is missing (`context.user`, for `if (!locals.user) error(401)`).

does.description: `route`: a route of the file's folder; `each`: a route for each property of the object it exports, at the folder's path followed by `path`, and the property named `default` at the folder's own path; `layout`: a chain member of the routes in its folder and below whose export takes `layouts`, outermost first; `use`: a chain member of every route.

path.description: For `each`: what follows the folder's path, where `{name}` is the property's name (`?/{name}`).

default.description: For `each`: the property that is the route at the folder's own path.

layouts.description: For `route`: the `layout` exports of its folder and those above apply.

receives.description: What the function receives first, when it is not the profile's `context` (`@sveltejs/kit#HandleInput` for `handle`).

files.description: Routes declared by files rather than calls: the folders of a route tree are its path, and the exports of each file what is served there (D32).

routes.description: The folder of the route tree, from the root of the package that uses the framework.

pattern.description: How a folder's name is written.

modules.description: The files of the route tree, by their name without the extension, and what each export declares.

hooks.description: Files of the package, by their path without the extension, whose exports apply to every route, in the order listed.

compose.description: Functions whose arguments are a chain, in order: `@sveltejs/kit/hooks#sequence`.

matchers.description: Where the matcher a parameter names (`[id=integer]`) is: a file, by its path without the extension where `{matcher}` is the matcher's name, and the export; or a property of an export, built by a function `through` lists.

remote.description: Modules, by the suffix of their name, whose exports built by these calls are routes of their own, at `path`: `$file` is the module's path, `$name` the export's.
